excluded_and_why.strategist span output (strategy + expla: app's stated intent. Reachable at trace scope, but the human graded the SONG, not the plan: on row 10459dc6 the strategy said 'classic rock' and was still labelled fail. Showing it invites the judge to grade the intent and score the app's own self-report.
excluded_and_why.spotify_search tool output: carries only track_id / artist / title / embed_url. No genre, era or style field anywhere in the trace - the genre knowledge the human used is the judge's own world knowledge, not trace content. Adds tokens, adds nothing.
excluded_and_why.span.evaluations (goal-completeness, pro: prior evaluator verdicts on the same trace. A prediction of the same property is leakage under the rubric, even though no human produced it.
excluded_and_why.annotation assessment / reviewer id / an: exist only because a human already graded the row.
excluded_and_why.reviewer reasoning: none exist on this queue (0 of 13), and would be leakage at prediction time regardless.

template_variables_verified.fidelity_gap: none - the local renderer shows exactly the root span input and output that {{span_input}}/{{span_output}} resolve to at span scope with root_spans_only.

rationale: follows_feedback asks whether the next recommendation respects what the user just said. Both halves of that question live on the root recommendation_cycle span and nowhere else: its input.value carries the previous song, the user's known/liked reaction, the verbatim feedback quote when there is one, and the session insight banner; its output.value carries the song the app chose. Nothing deeper in the tree (strategist plan, Spotify tool results, three OpenAI llm calls) adds evidence about the label - they add the app's intent and opaque track ids. Because the same two fields are what {{span_input}} and {{span_output}} resolve to on a root-span-scoped evaluator, the judge is fitted on precisely what the deployed evaluator will see.
